Graphics Display Line Thickness

Configure the line thickness of the displayed graphic by a pixel count (1 to 64. Default: 2).

Setting Items of [String]

You can specify parameters by the result data of a different tool so as to display a graphic in accordance with the result data.

Configure a plain text to be displayed and the display position of the plain text.

Count Configure the number of graphics to be displayed (0 to 30000. Default: 1). String

Enter a plain text of 128 characters (64 double byte characters) or less to be displayed in the camera image.

Tab and linefeed cannot be used. Space can be used. Position X

Configure the X coordinate (: 16383.000 to 16383.000. Default: 260.000) of the position where the plain text is to be displayed.

Configure the Y coordinate (: 16383.000 to 16383.000. Default: 240.000) of the position where the plain text is to be displayed.

Select a display type for the plain text to be displayed on the camera image.

Display Type 0 Display Type 1 (default)

If you set [Display Type] with reference to the result data of a different tool, you can

switch between different graphics to display them in accordance with the result data. When the result data is [0]: The graphic of [Display Type 0] is displayed.

When the result data is [1]: The graphic of [Display Type 1] is displayed.

Specifications: Expansion I/O unit

*1 The input COM and output COM terminals are independent. *2 The KV-N8EXR has two C1 output terminals and two C2 output terminals, but each pair of terminals is shared internally. Error Number: 13401; Error Messages: Unable to make the terminal output due to a full output buffer.; Cause: The output buffer for output via the terminal is full.; Remedy: Reduce the amount of data to be output through the parallel/terminal outputs, so the data is output at a faster rate than it builds up. Or, extend the time between triggers/processing to allow for data to be output. Note: Results data is not written when the buffer is full.
Error Number: 13402; Error Messages: The delay of the handshake control causes skipping of the  I/O terminal output.; Cause: As the amount of data output overflows the buffer, data output is suspended partially.; Remedy: • Check that handshake is controlled properly. • Clear the data in the output buffer using the TEST terminal (bit) or reset input.

4-24 LJ-X UM_US

Head Settings (When Using the LJ: X Series Head)

Head settings Installation Correction Configures data processing for detected profiles. Wide Combination

Links the height images/ shading(contrast) images of 2 heads in the X direction, and captures them as a single image. If the linking points deviate, adjust them with the shift/ offset.

Profile Adjustment Image horizontal flip Flips an entire height image obtained from 2 heads horizontally.

Invert X Direction

Flip the height image in the X direction. Enable when the head installation direction is reversed. With 2 heads, the image is reversed for each head.

Flip the height image in the Z direction. The image is reversed for each head.

Flip the height image in the Y direction. The image is reversed for each head.

Shift X Direction

Offsets the height image/ shading(contrast) image in the X direction to correct the deviation. Use when the head's installation point shifts from the standard

point, or when the position linked by wide link shifts. Z Direction

Offsets the profile in the Z direction to correct a deviation. Use when the head's installation point shifts from the standard point, or when the position linked by wide link shifts.

External | Capture images in response to trigger inputs from the mouse or trigger signals sent from an external device. Captures processing only once for each trigger input.
Internal | Sets the trigger cycle and captures images in response to trigger signals that are generated periodically. Processing can be repeated without the external trigger input

External Terminal | TRG triggers input through the allocated external I/ O terminal.
Mouse | It is the trigger input by clicking "Measurement execution" with the mouse.
RS-232C | It is the trigger input by command via RS-232C.

Time Delay | Set the line scan interval in hours.
Specify | Set the line scan interval with the encoder count.
Encoder |

Sheet-fed | Captures one slice of the height image/shading (contrast) image. Imaging is initiated via the input of the TRG signal and halted when capturing is completed for the specified number of lines or when the EXT signal is input.
Continuous acquisition | Continuously captures the height image/shading (contrast) image. Imaging is initiated via the input of the TRG signal and halted via the input of the EXTsignal.Specifythetotalnumberoflineswhen importing a specified number of lines and inspecting a long workpiece.
Sheet-fed (auto part detection) | Continuously captures the height image/shading (contrast) image. Images are imported when a workpiece is captured at the specified height or with the specified shading.
NOTICE | When Sheet-fed (auto part detection) is set, the laser beam is emitted at all times. If capturing is interrupted by the EXT signal, laser on terminal or TE command after the trigger is confirmed, the partially captured image is generally discarded, but in some cases the image may be captured as a black image and misjudged by the system. Do not interrupt capturing during operation.

* WORD: Unsigned 16-bit integer DWORD: Unsigned 32-bit integer The unit of processing time is msec.

If two or more errors are occurring at the same time, the error code of the highest priority error will be displayed.

The first occurred warning code will be displayed.

A checksum can be used to monitor whether the sensor settings have been modified by a third party.

The checksum can check whether program is switched.

The checksum will remain unchanged even if you change the IP address, subnet mask, default gateway or port number of the IV4 Series.

For the number of remaining buffers, refer to 'Reading out the status result (handshake control: [Enable]; Preliminary capture: [Disable])' (page 9-78) .

The upper limit value of the result No. is 32767. If the maximum value is exceeded, it will go back to 0 and start counting up again.

The result No. will also count the judgment process counts that were skipped due to the data I/O cycle settings.

If the number of triggers or the number of times of the completion of result output transfer exceeds the upper limit, the counting up starts from 0 again.

The number of OK triggers, the number of NG triggers, and the number of trigger errors stop counting up at the upper limit.

A reset will occur in the following conditions: When [Statistics reset] is input When a tool is added/deleted/copied

Operation Symbol/Output Item Comparison Table (Measured Value/Judgment Value) Operation Symbol/Output Item Comparison Table (Measured Value/Judgment Value)

ST (Reference value): Measured value for the reference image calculated during setting.

MS (Measured value): The measured result data that is output.

JG (Judgment value): Judgment result (OK=0,NG=1).

AB (Absolute measured value): Measured value before specifying the origin. When Position Correction is used, it is the value before adjustment.

HL (Upper limit): The upper limit used for judgment.

LL (Lower limit): The lower limit used for judgment.

Items that can use label specification are only MS (measured value) and AB (absolute measured value).

When the output is set, the selection is automatically set to [MS]. Items for which a decimal number (with any number of digits) is listed under Format of measurement data are handled as decimal data in PLC-Link, EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, and EtherCAT. For details, check 'Decimal Point' for each communication method in 'Chapter 9 Communication control' (Page 9-1).

For an item with the symbol * shown at the end, the measured value correction function is available. For details, see 'Correction of measured values' (Page 5-12).

Operation Symbol/Output Item Comparison Table (Measured Value/Judgment Value) Operation Symbol/Output Item Comparison Table (Measured Value/Judgment Value)

ST (Reference value): Measured value for the reference image calculated during setting.

MS (Measured value): The measured result data that is output.

JG (Judgment value): Judgment result (OK=0,NG=1).

AB (Absolute measured value): Measured value before specifying the origin. When Position Correction is used, it is the value before adjustment.

HL (Upper limit): The upper limit used for judgment.

LL (Lower limit): The lower limit used for judgment.

Items that can use label specification are only MS (measured value) and AB (absolute measured value).

When the output is set, the selection is automatically set to [MS]. Items for which a decimal number (with any number of digits) is listed under Format of measurement data are handled as decimal data in PLC-Link, EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, and EtherCAT. For details, check 'Decimal Point' for each communication method in 'Chapter 9 Communication control' (Page 9-1).

For an item with the symbol * shown at the end, the measured value correction function is available. For details, see 'Correction of measured values' (Page 5-12).

Operation Symbol/Output Item Comparison Table (Measured Value/Judgment Value) Operation Symbol/Output Item Comparison Table (Measured Value/Judgment Value)

ST (Reference value): Measured value for the reference image calculated during setting.

MS (Measured value): The measured result data that is output.

JG (Judgment value): Judgment result (OK=0,NG=1).

AB (Absolute measured value): Measured value before specifying the origin. When Position Correction is used, it is the value before adjustment.

HL (Upper limit): The upper limit used for judgment.

LL (Lower limit): The lower limit used for judgment.

Items that can use label specification are only MS (measured value) and AB (absolute measured value).

When the output is set, the selection is automatically set to [MS]. Items for which a decimal number (with any number of digits) is listed under Format of measurement data are handled as decimal data in PLC-Link, EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, and EtherCAT. For details, check 'Decimal Point' for each communication method in 'Chapter 9 Communication control' (Page 9-1).

For an item with the symbol * shown at the end, the measured value correction function is available. For details, see 'Correction of measured values' (Page 5-12).

Operation Symbol/Output Item Comparison Table (Measured Value/Judgment Value) Operation Symbol/Output Item Comparison Table (Measured Value/Judgment Value)

ST (Reference value): Measured value for the reference image calculated during setting.

MS (Measured value): The measured result data that is output.

JG (Judgment value): Judgment result (OK=0,NG=1).

AB (Absolute measured value): Measured value before specifying the origin. When Position Correction is used, it is the value before adjustment.

HL (Upper limit): The upper limit used for judgment.

LL (Lower limit): The lower limit used for judgment.

Items that can use label specification are only MS (measured value) and AB (absolute measured value).

When the output is set, the selection is automatically set to [MS]. Items for which a decimal number (with any number of digits) is listed under Format of measurement data are handled as decimal data in PLC-Link, EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, and EtherCAT. For details, check 'Decimal Point' for each communication method in 'Chapter 9 Communication control' (Page 9-1).

For an item with the symbol * shown at the end, the measured value correction function is available. For details, see 'Correction of measured values' (Page 5-12).

Operation Symbol/Output Item Comparison Table (Measured Value/Judgment Value) Operation Symbol/Output Item Comparison Table (Measured Value/Judgment Value)

ST (Reference value): Measured value for the reference image calculated during setting.

MS (Measured value): The measured result data that is output.

JG (Judgment value): Judgment result (OK=0,NG=1).

AB (Absolute measured value): Measured value before specifying the origin. When Position Correction is used, it is the value before adjustment.

HL (Upper limit): The upper limit used for judgment.

LL (Lower limit): The lower limit used for judgment.

Items that can use label specification are only MS (measured value) and AB (absolute measured value).

When the output is set, the selection is automatically set to [MS]. Items for which a decimal number (with any number of digits) is listed under Format of measurement data are handled as decimal data in PLC-Link, EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, and EtherCAT. For details, check 'Decimal Point' for each communication method in 'Chapter 9 Communication control' (Page 9-1).

For an item with the symbol * shown at the end, the measured value correction function is available. For details, see 'Correction of measured values' (Page 5-12).

Operation Symbol/Output Item Comparison Table (Measured Value/Judgment Value) Operation Symbol/Output Item Comparison Table (Measured Value/Judgment Value)

ST (Reference value): Measured value for the reference image calculated during setting.

MS (Measured value): The measured result data that is output.

JG (Judgment value): Judgment result (OK=0,NG=1).

AB (Absolute measured value): Measured value before specifying the origin. When Position Correction is used, it is the value before adjustment.

HL (Upper limit): The upper limit used for judgment.

LL (Lower limit): The lower limit used for judgment.

Items that can use label specification are only MS (measured value) and AB (absolute measured value).

When the output is set, the selection is automatically set to [MS]. Items for which a decimal number (with any number of digits) is listed under Format of measurement data are handled as decimal data in PLC-Link, EtherNet/IP, PROFINET, and EtherCAT. For details, check 'Decimal Point' for each communication method in 'Chapter 9 Communication control' (Page 9-1).

For an item with the symbol * shown at the end, the measured value correction function is available. For details, see 'Correction of measured values' (Page 5-12).

z Reset Status Output on Clear Error Execution  Enable

Resets status output when clear error is input. Judgment-related outputs and errors will be turned off until the judgment result by the next trigger input is output.

If a PC, control panel, or display expansion unit is connected, the image used for judgment will be reset and the [Waiting for trigger] screen will appear.

 Disable (default) Does not reset status output when clear error is input. Judgment output cannot be reset with this function via the field network.

To do a reset via the field network, use [Status result/Buffer clear request]. 'Chapter 9 Connecting to a Network' (page 9-1)
